Rugged tablet for Joblogic

Joblogic is a field service management system for service contractors, built and sold from the UK by Tracer Management Systems Limited, which trades as Joblogic and gives a Birmingham address on its site. The vendor describes it as connecting jobs, engineers, assets, compliance, quotes and invoices in one system, and lists mechanical and electrical, HVAC and refrigeration, fire and security, facilities management and plumbing and heating among more than 30 trades it covers. The office plans and schedules work in the web product; engineers receive and complete that work in the Joblogic Mobile app.

The mobile app is where the site work happens. The vendor's Google Play listing says engineers capture time sheets, notes, parts, expenses, mileage, photos and signatures, and that bespoke forms can replace risk assessments, gas and electrical certificates, equipment service sheets and customer satisfaction forms. Its user guide documents a Scan option that opens the camera to find assets by QR code or barcode, and its FAQ says the app can be used without signal. That is a device that lives in a van, goes up ladders, into plant rooms and loft spaces, and gets handed to a customer for a signature, which is where a consumer tablet with a glass back and no sealing tends to fail early.

This page sets out what Joblogic publishes about the devices its app runs on, which Tuga rugged tablets meet those published requirements, where the Windows option fits and where it does not, and how a UK contractor can buy a single trial unit before committing to a fleet.

Requirements

What Joblogic needs from a device

Each item below comes from Tracer Management Systems Limited (trading as Joblogic)'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 7.0 or later with a minimum of 4GB RAM

    The vendor's System Requirements page (last updated 29 September 2026) states that the mobile app runs on Android 7.0 or above with a minimum of 4GB RAM, and on iOS 15.0 or above for Apple devices. No storage figure is published. An older FAQ page on joblogic.com still quotes Android 4.0 upwards; the System Requirements page is the current figure and matches the Google Play listing. Source: support.joblogic.com

  • Android app from Google Play, for phones and tablets

    The Android app is published on Google Play as Joblogic (package com.tracer.joblogic, developer JobLogic Limited). When checked on 15 October 2026 the listing showed version 1.186.2, updated 5 October 2026, with a minimum API level of 24 (Android 7.0), and device chips for Phone and Tablet. The vendor's user guide tells Android users to download the app from Google Play. Source: play.google.com

  • Offline working, with a connection needed to receive new visits

    The vendor's FAQ says Joblogic Mobile can be used without signal when installed from Google Play or the App Store, and that once offline working is enabled engineers can log jobs and quotes offline. It also says an internet connection is required to download new visit details to the device in the first place, and that jobs can take up to 10 minutes to arrive on a device using the offline version. The user guide adds a manual sync option under Status. The vendor does not publish how much data is cached on the device. Source: joblogic.com

  • Asset scanning by QR code or barcode, through the camera

    The user guide says the Scan option can be used to search for Joblogic assets by QR code or barcode, and that it opens the device camera. Codes that are not already set up against an asset in Joblogic return no result. No support for a dedicated hardware scan engine or an external scanner is documented, so on any device the scan path is the camera. Source: support.joblogic.com

  • Photos, attachments and customer signatures in the app

    The user guide documents an attachments area where engineers add photos and files or take a photo with the camera, including several images at once, and receipt photos on expenses. At completion the customer can be asked to sign, and the engineer can sign too; depending on back office settings a signature may be mandatory. Job forms appear once the engineer marks themselves On Site, and a partly completed form is saved only up to the last finished page. Source: support.joblogic.com

  • GPS tracking module and device settings for background running

    The vendor's job tracking page says workers can be monitored from the office through a GPS tracking module. The user guide's first run prompts cover Low Power Mode, letting the app run in the background, an overlay setting and biometric login, and its View On Map route works only with signal and a correctly set up address. No GNSS accuracy or location hardware requirement is published. Source: joblogic.com

  • Windows: no Windows mobile app, web product in a browser

    The System Requirements page states that Joblogic is not available on Windows phones, and no native Windows app is published. The web product is described as working across all modern browsers as long as they support HTML 5, with a recommendation to accept browser updates. No specific browser list or version numbers are published. Source: support.joblogic.com

Worth knowing. Joblogic has no Windows app and says it is not available on Windows phones, so the Tuga W10 only runs the web product in a browser. The engineer features the vendor documents (camera asset scanning, offline working, photos, signatures and job forms) are in the mobile app, so a W10 suits an office or workshop desk, not an engineer on site. On the Android side, the only scan method the vendor documents is the camera, with no dedicated scan engine or external scanner support published, so the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine is not a documented Joblogic input. The vendor publishes no storage figure, no screen-size guidance and no NFC or RFID support, so the NFC radio on the A10, A8 and A6 should not be treated as a Joblogic feature. The vendor's GPS tracking module is described from the office side only; it does not publish what location accuracy it needs from a device.
Setting up

Getting Joblogic running

  1. Ask your Joblogic administrator to set the engineer up as a mobile user in your Joblogic account and to enable offline working if your team needs it.
  2. On the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, open Google Play and install Joblogic (package com.tracer.joblogic, developer JobLogic Limited), then sign in with the engineer's details.
  3. Work through the first run prompts the user guide describes: Low Power Mode, letting the app run in the background, the overlay setting and biometric login. Allow camera and location access so the Scan option and the GPS tracking module can work.
  4. Before the first job without signal, keep the device online long enough to download the engineer's visit details. The vendor says new jobs can take up to 10 minutes to arrive on a device using the offline version, and the Status screen has a manual sync option.
  5. Test the Scan option against an asset whose QR code or barcode is already set up in Joblogic, and complete a test job with photos and a signature, before rolling out to the team.
  6. On a Tuga W10, open the Joblogic web product in Edge or Chrome and keep the browser updated, as the vendor recommends. Use it for office work; it will not run the mobile app.
  7. For the A10 and A8, fit the vehicle mounting dock in the van; for the A10 and W10, add the charging dock where devices live overnight; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out.

Questions

Joblogic on a Tuga device

Joblogic publishes a requirement of Android 7.0 or above with a minimum of 4GB RAM, and its Google Play listing gives a minimum API level of 24 (Android 7.0). The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 with Google Play and has 8GB RAM and 128GB storage, so it meets each published figure. The Tuga A8 (Android 12, 6GB RAM) also meets them, and the Tuga A6 (Android 15, 4GB RAM) meets them with no RAM headroom. We do not describe any device as certified or tested by Joblogic; these are the vendor's published requirements set against the device specifications.

The vendor's FAQ says Joblogic Mobile can be used without signal when installed from Google Play, and that with offline working enabled engineers can log jobs and quotes offline. A connection is needed to download new visit details in the first place, and the vendor says jobs can take up to 10 minutes to arrive on a device using the offline version. The A10, A8 and A6 all run the Google Play app. A Tuga W10 can only use the web product in a browser, and the vendor does not document offline working there.

Joblogic's user guide documents a Scan option that opens the camera to find assets by QR code or barcode, provided the code is already set up in Joblogic. The A10, A8 and A6 all have a 13MP rear camera with flash, and on each of them scanning runs through the camera via the app. The A6 also has a Zebra 2D scan engine, but the vendor documents no dedicated scan engine or external scanner support, so do not buy it for that reason alone.

Both meet Joblogic's published requirements. The A10 has more RAM (8GB against 6GB), a sharper 1920 x 1200 screen for multi-page forms and certificates, IP68 against IP67, and MIL-STD-810H, which the A8 does not have. The A8 has a 1000 nit screen against the A10's 350 nits, a removable battery, VESA mount points, and costs £379 against £449. Engineers who mostly work outdoors or do long days away from a charger may prefer the A8; those filling in long forms or working in wetter, harder conditions are better served by the A10.
